title: Examination timetabling: algorithmic strategies and applications
venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
key_finding: Describes the authors' computerised examination timetabling system EXAMINE and investigates and compares several algorithmic strategies for the problem. Computational results are reported on randomly generated problems and some real problems.
limitations: Pre-window foundational original; abstract does not name the individual strategies or give quantitative results.
algorithm: Several algorithmic strategies within the EXAMINE system (not itemised in abstract)
benchmark: Randomly generated and real problems (abstract). Later papers (e.g. B06, B14) cite this paper as the origin of the uncapacitated Carter/Toronto formulation/dataset.
notes: All draft fields confirmed via OpenAlex. Not OA.

title: A survey of search methodologies and automated system development for examination timetabling
key_finding: Critical survey of roughly a decade of exam timetabling research, highlighting hybridised search methodologies and methods that raise the level of generality (e.g. hyper-heuristics). It clarifies confusion caused by different versions of benchmark datasets circulating under the same name and proposes a renaming of the widely studied datasets, indicating which papers used which version.
limitations: Survey (no new algorithm); coverage ends c.2008; pre-window.
algorithm: Survey of exam timetabling methodologies
benchmark: Discusses public benchmark exam datasets (Toronto/Carter versions) and their renaming
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2008 (online 29 Oct 2008); journal issue Feb 2009, so 2009 is correct for citation. Abstract from Springer page.

title: Setting the research agenda in automated timetabling: the second International Timetabling Competition
key_finding: Describes the Second International Timetabling Competition (ITC2007/TTC2007), launched August 2007, which supplied real-world problem models with substantial practical constraints in three tracks reflecting variations of higher-education timetabling. It presents the background, competition structure and the winning techniques.
limitations: Competition description; pre-window. Abstract text was returned paraphrased by the retrieval tool, so wording should be checked against the publisher page before quoting.
algorithm: Competition definition (no single algorithm)
benchmark: Defines ITC2007 (examination track is one of three tracks)
notes: Full author list: 9 authors (draft 'McCollum et al.'). OpenAlex publication_year=2009 (online); print Feb 2010 per Crossref.

title: Educational timetabling: problems, benchmarks, and state-of-the-art results
key_finding: Surveys educational timetabling with a focus on 'standard' formulations and their benchmark instances, identifying six such formulations and discussing their relevance and usability. It reports main state-of-the-art results on the selected benchmarks (upper and lower bounds, search techniques, running times).
limitations: Survey; no new algorithm.
algorithm: Survey of formulations, benchmarks and state-of-the-art results
benchmark: Six formulations incl. uncapacitated exam timetabling (Toronto/Carter) and ITC-2007 examination track (also PE-CTT, CB-CTT, XHSTT, ITC-2019) per ScienceDirect page
notes: OpenAlex DOI record is merged with the arXiv preprint (type=preprint, source=arXiv, biblio null, year 2022); journal details 308(1):1-18, July 2023 confirmed via Crossref and ScienceDirect. Published OA under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

title: A survey of solution methodologies for exam timetabling problems
key_finding: Survey describing the exam timetabling problem, its variants, constraints and benchmark datasets, and reviewing solution methods from 2012 to 2023: mathematical optimisation, heuristics, metaheuristics, hyper-heuristics, hybrid approaches and matheuristics. It closes with review findings and potential research directions.
limitations: Survey; no new algorithm or experiments.
algorithm: Survey (2012-2023 methods)
benchmark: Reviews benchmark datasets (not itemised in abstract)
notes: Draft author list/order wrong ('Siew, Goh, Sabar, Abdullah, Kendall?'): correct order is Siew, Sze, Goh, Kendall, Sabar, Abdullah (Sze was missing). DOI was missing in draft; now 10.1109/ACCESS.2024.3378054. Open access.

title: Two-stage multi-neighborhood simulated annealing for uncapacitated examination timetabling
key_finding: Proposes simulated annealing for the classical uncapacitated formulation of Carter et al. (1996), combining many neighbourhoods with a principled tuning procedure on artificial training instances. On real-world benchmarks it improves on all state-of-the-art methods on most instances at equal running time; an ablation analysis identifies the most important neighbourhoods, and instances, solutions and source code are released.
limitations: Static problem only; tuning on artificial instances; no disruption/repair setting.
algorithm: Two-stage multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing with statistical parameter tuning
benchmark: Uncapacitated Carter/Toronto formulation ('real-world benchmarks'); plus a new dataset translated from other exam formulations
notes: Pages is article number 105300 (Aug 2021). OpenAlex abstract null; abstract taken from ScienceDirect. OpenAlex reports is_oa=true with ScienceDirect URL.

title: A fast simulated annealing algorithm for the examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Proposes FastSA, an SA variant in which an exam is only moved/evaluated if it had accepted moves in the preceding temperature bin (ten bins), since exams with no accepted moves tend to be 'crystallised'. This yields fewer evaluations than standard SA (abstract text from Semantic Scholar reports '17% less evaluations, on average') while remaining competitive on ITC 2007 instances.
limitations: Abstract does not report Toronto results; capacitated ITC2007 focus.
algorithm: FastSA (simulated annealing with move-evaluation pruning); saturation-degree construction with Conflict-Based Statistics
benchmark: ITC 2007
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2018 (online); volume 122 is May 2019. Authors confirmed.

title: A robust simulated annealing based examination timetabling system
key_finding: Develops an examination scheduling system solved in two simulated-annealing phases: the first seeks a feasible solution and the second improves secondary objectives and soft constraints. Different parameter and modelling choices are compared on a test-bed derived from several institutions, giving a robust system across problem specifications.
limitations: Pre-window foundational original; datasets are institution-specific rather than the Toronto set.
algorithm: Two-phase simulated annealing
benchmark: Test-bed of problems derived from data from a variety of institutions (abstract)
notes: All draft fields confirmed.

title: A time-predefined local search approach to exam timetabling problems
key_finding: Presents two local search variants in which run time is an input parameter: a time-predefined simulated annealing and an adapted great deluge method. Experiments show they significantly outperform previous best results on a range of benchmark exam timetabling problems, at the price of increased execution time.
limitations: Pre-window; quality-time trade-off (longer runs).
algorithm: Time-predefined simulated annealing; great deluge
benchmark: 'Range of benchmark exam timetabling problems' (not named in abstract)
notes: All draft fields confirmed.

title: The late acceptance hill-climbing heuristic
key_finding: Introduces Late Acceptance Hill-Climbing (LAHC), a local search that accepts a non-improving candidate if its cost is better than the cost a fixed number of iterations earlier, with a single parameter. On travelling salesman and exam timetabling benchmarks it was compared with simulated annealing, threshold accepting and great deluge and performed better on most instances, particularly larger ones.
limitations: General-purpose metaheuristic; exam instances not named in retrieved abstract; abstract partly paraphrased by retrieval tool.
algorithm: Late acceptance hill-climbing
benchmark: Exam timetabling benchmarks (not named in retrieved text) and TSP
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2016 (online July 2016); print issue April 2017 (Crossref). in_window=true by issue date; false if online date used.

title: A graph-based hyper-heuristic for educational timetabling problems
key_finding: Uses tabu search to search permutations of graph colouring constructive heuristics, which are then used to build exam and course timetables, including a two-stage multi-stage variant. Results on exam and course benchmarks are within the range of the best reported in the literature.
limitations: Pre-window; constructive focus.
algorithm: Graph-based hyper-heuristic: tabu search over sequences of graph-colouring heuristics
benchmark: Exam and course benchmark problems; ScienceDirect page cites Carter et al. (1996) exam problems
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2005 (online); issue Jan 2007. OA copy available.

title: An informed genetic algorithm for the examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Two-phase genetic algorithm: phase one produces timetables meeting hard constraints, phase two reduces soft-constraint cost, with domain heuristics guiding evolution. On the 13 Carter benchmarks it is comparable to, and sometimes better than, other evolutionary techniques.
limitations: Pre-window.
algorithm: Two-phase heuristic-informed genetic algorithm
benchmark: Carter (Toronto) benchmarks, 13 problems
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2009 (online); issue March 2010.

title: Ant algorithms for the exam timetabling problem
venue: Practice and Theory of Automated Timetabling VI (PATAT 2006), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, eds. Burke, E.K. & Rudová, H.
key_finding: Presents two ant colony approaches for exam timetabling, a Max-Min and an ANTCOL approach, and compares them with other heuristics on the Toronto benchmarks. Despite some shortcomings, ANTCOL was found to be among the best algorithms then in use.
limitations: Pre-window; conference chapter.
algorithm: Ant colony optimisation (Max-Min Ant System, ANTCOL)
benchmark: Toronto
notes: All draft fields confirmed (LNCS 3867, 2007).

title: Memetic techniques for examination timetabling
key_finding: Uses harmony search, treated as a memetic algorithm variant, to test 17 scenarios combining recombination, randomness and neighbourhood structures for uncapacitated exam timetabling; combining all three gives the best results. Compared with 22 methods on the Carter dataset, it exceeded previous results on 2 of 12 instances.
limitations: Pre-window; best on only 2 of 12 instances.
algorithm: Harmony search as a memetic algorithm
benchmark: Carter et al. (1996) / Toronto, 12 instances
notes: Online Nov 2013; issue July 2014 (OpenAlex year 2013).

title: An adaptive artificial bee colony and late-acceptance hill-climbing algorithm for examination timetabling
key_finding: Modifies artificial bee colony with a disruptive selection strategy for population diversity and a self-adaptive choice of neighbourhood structures, and hybridises it with late-acceptance hill-climbing. Both the disruptive-selection variant and the hybrid outperform the basic ABC on exam timetabling.
limitations: Pre-window; retrieved abstract (partly paraphrased by tool) does not name the datasets.
algorithm: Artificial bee colony + late-acceptance hill-climbing
notes: Online Dec 2013; issue June 2014 (OpenAlex year 2013). Benchmark not confirmed from abstract.

title: An investigation of fuzzy multiple heuristic orderings in the construction of university examination timetables
key_finding: Uses fuzzy methods to combine pairs of three single construction (graph-colouring ordering) heuristics to decide exam insertion order. On 12 benchmark problems the fuzzy combinations gave lower penalty than any single heuristic on all 12 (and the best published constructive result on one), with less backtracking.
limitations: Pre-window; construction only.
algorithm: Fuzzy combination of constructive ordering heuristics
benchmark: '12 well-known benchmark problems' (not named in abstract)
notes: OpenAlex publication_year=2008 (online); issue April 2009.

title: A hyperheuristic approach to examination timetabling problems: benchmarks and a new problem from practice
limitations: Abstract could not be retrieved (OpenAlex/Crossref/Semantic Scholar null; Springer page rate-limited; Lirias timed out). Content claims must be checked against the paper.
algorithm: Hyperheuristic (from title only)
notes: Metadata confirmed via OpenAlex and Crossref: online 17 Nov 2011, print Feb 2012.

title: A column generation approach for solving the examination-timetabling problem
key_finding: Student-centric exam timetabling that allows multiple versions of an exam, solved with two column-generation models (exam schedule per student group; mask schedule per group) with heuristic column selection instead of branch-and-price. Applied to KU Leuven campus Brussels and two literature datasets.
limitations: Published 16 Aug 2016, just before the recency window; heuristic column selection, no optimality proof.
algorithm: Column generation (two master/pricing decompositions)
benchmark: Real university (KU Leuven Brussels) plus two literature datasets; ScienceDirect page names Toronto sta83 and yor83
notes: All draft fields confirmed.

title: Feature-based tuning of single-stage simulated annealing for examination timetabling
key_finding: Single-stage simulated annealing for the ITC2007 examination formulation that searches infeasible space with penalties, plus a statistically principled, feature-based parameter tuning that generalises better to unseen instances than a one-size-fits-all setting. Properly tuned, it competes with all state-of-the-art specialised solvers; a larger set of artificial instances is published.
limitations: Capacitated ITC2007 formulation, not Toronto.
algorithm: Single-stage simulated annealing with feature-based parameter tuning
benchmark: ITC2007 examination track; new artificial instances
notes: OpenAlex year 2015 (online 23 Nov 2015); issue May 2017. in_window=true by issue date only.

title: A proven optimal result for a benchmark instance of the uncapacitated examination timetabling problem
venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on the Practice and Theory of Automated Timetabling (PATAT 2022), Volume III, Leuven, Belgium, 30 Aug-2 Sep 2022 (eds. De Causmaecker, P., Özcan, E., Vanden Berghe, G.; ISBN 978-0-9929984-5-5)
key_finding: Proves optimality of the best known solution for Carter's sta83 instance by decomposing the problem into three parts, each closed by a different approach (MIP with CPLEX, clique-based enumeration and lower bounds). The paper reports the optimum as 95947 (157.0327 per student) and also gives optimal solutions for subproblems and two new best known solutions.
limitations: Single small instance proven optimal; heavy computation (several hours); proceedings paper without DOI.
algorithm: Problem decomposition + mixed integer programming + enumeration/lower bounds
benchmark: Toronto/Carter (sta83); subproblems from public datasets
notes: PATAT proceedings have no DOI. Author order here is Dimitsas, Nastos, Valouxis, Alefragis, Gogos. A journal version exists (J. Scheduling 28(2):183-194, 2025, DOI 10.1007/s10951-024-00805-0, author order Dimitsas, Gogos, Valouxis, Nastos, Alefragis) - see B26g. The draft B24 DOI actually resolves to this journal version.

title: Addressing examination timetabling problem using a partial exams approach in constructive and improvement
key_finding: Schedules exams in partial batches: each batch is placed with partial graph-heuristic orderings and improved with a modified great deluge (PGH-mGD) before the next batch, instead of building a full timetable first. On ITC2007 and the uncapacitated Toronto dataset it gives solutions competitive with published approaches.
limitations: MDPI journal; results described as competitive rather than best.
algorithm: Partial graph-heuristic orderings + modified great deluge (PGH-mGD)
benchmark: ITC2007 and Toronto
notes: Article number 46. All draft fields confirmed. Open access.

title: The examination timetabling problem at Universiti Malaysia Pahang: comparison of a constructive heuristic with an existing software solution
key_finding: Formally defines a real-world capacitated exam timetabling problem at Universiti Malaysia Pahang with new constraints (distance between rooms, splitting exams across rooms). A constructive heuristic gives better solutions than the university's existing software and meets all hard constraints, which the existing system does not.
limitations: Pre-window; single institution.
algorithm: Constructive heuristic
benchmark: Real university (UMP)
notes: All draft fields confirmed.

title: Real-life examination timetabling
key_finding: Presents exam timetabling at a large American university, solved with an approach based on the ITC 2007 winning solver integrated into the open-source UniTime system. Nine real-world datasets are made public (results given for four), and splitting some exams across periods is studied to reduce student conflicts.
limitations: Issue date June 2016, before the window; single institution.
algorithm: ITC2007-winning local search solver within UniTime
benchmark: Real university (nine public real-world datasets)
notes: OpenAlex year 2014 (online 9 Aug 2014); issue June 2016.

title: On the computation of robust examination timetables: methods and experimental results
key_finding: Defines examination timetabling from curricula (before registration data exist) and introduces three robustness measures for the uncertainty of this model, analysed with multi-objective simulated annealing and Pareto front approximations. A case study shows that, without significant quality loss, the chance of needing rescheduling once exact numbers are known is significantly reduced.
limitations: Curriculum-based (pre-registration) model; proactive robustness, not reactive repair.
algorithm: Multi-objective simulated annealing with three robustness measures
benchmark: Case study (real university setting; dataset not named in abstract)
notes: Draft DOI 10.1007/s10951-024-00805-0 WRONG (it is Dimitsas et al., see B20/B26g); correct DOI 10.1007/s10951-024-00815-y. Draft 'Bassimir et al.' = 2 authors (Bassimir, Wanka). Online 7 Nov 2024, issue April 2025. Open access CC BY.

title: Hybridization and artificial intelligence in optimizing university examination timetabling problem: a systematic review
key_finding: Systematic review of heuristic, metaheuristic, mixed integer programming, hybrid and hyper-heuristic approaches, and the role of AI, for university exam timetabling. Gaps identified include the level of hybridisation between population-based and local search, design of the initial solution, balancing multiple stakeholders, and phase-wise partial solution construction.
limitations: Education-research journal rather than OR/CS venue; OpenAlex abstract reconstruction is garbled, so wording is approximate.
algorithm: Systematic literature review
notes: DOI found (draft 'check DOI'): 10.1002/rev3.70071; article e70071; online 20 May 2025, issue Aug 2025. Open access.

title: A cellular memetic algorithm for the examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Cellular evolutionary algorithm (population in a cellular structure for diversity) hybridised with threshold acceptance local search, using feasibility-preserving recombination and local search operators. A low threshold-decreasing rate was needed; it found four new upper bounds on Toronto and three on ITC 2007.
limitations: Static timetabling; no disruption handling.
algorithm: Cellular memetic algorithm (cellular EA + threshold acceptance)
benchmark: Toronto and ITC 2007
notes: Discovered; verified via OpenAlex and ScienceDirect. Family: evolutionary/memetic.

title: Fairness in examination timetabling: student preferences and extended formulations
key_finding: A student survey showed fairness within a cohort (equitable distribution of preparation time) is a major concern, so fairness is added as a new objective to standard exam models, making the problem multi-objective. A multi-stage multi-objective approach with weighted Tchebycheff scalarisation produced high-quality timetables trading off standard soft constraints against fairness.
limitations: Multi-objective extension; not a repair/disruption setting.
algorithm: Multi-stage multi-objective approach with weighted Tchebycheff scalarisation
benchmark: 'Several real-world examination data models' (abstract); ScienceDirect page names Carter, ITC 2007 and Yeditepe
notes: Discovered; verified via OpenAlex and ScienceDirect. Family: multi-objective / stakeholder-centred. OA copy.

title: Automated generation of constructive ordering heuristics for educational timetabling
key_finding: Generation constructive hyper-heuristics evolve arithmetic heuristics (genetic programming) and hierarchical heuristics (GP, GA, random combinations) to replace hand-made graph colouring ordering heuristics. The evolved heuristics performed much better than the existing graph colouring heuristics; arithmetic heuristics were more effective for exam timetabling, hierarchical ones for curriculum-based course timetabling.
limitations: Benchmarks not named in abstract or Springer page text; construction phase only.
algorithm: Generation hyper-heuristics (genetic programming / genetic algorithm) evolving graph-colouring ordering heuristics
notes: Discovered. Online 4 Sep 2017; issue April 2019 (OpenAlex year 2017). Abstract via Semantic Scholar API. OpenAlex oa_url redirects to a Nottingham repository 'not found' page. Family: hyper-heuristic / learned constructive heuristics.

title: Lower bounds and compact mathematical formulations for spacing soft constraints for university examination timetabling problems
key_finding: For ITC2007 spacing soft constraints (students sitting more than one exam per day), proposes a generic lower-bound model and compact formulations with O(number of exams) equations instead of quadratic. Results improve on earlier lower bounds, and the compact models outperform existing formulations.
limitations: Lower bounds only for spacing constraints; not a full solver.
algorithm: Integer programming formulations and lower bounds
benchmark: ITC2007 (abstract); ScienceDirect page also names Yeditepe
notes: Discovered; verified via OpenAlex and ScienceDirect. Family: exact / mathematical programming.

title: Exact and metaheuristic methods for a real-world examination timetabling problem
key_finding: For a rich real-world Italian exam problem (two-part exams, multi-room exams, period and room unavailabilities and preferences), compares a CP model (MiniZinc/Gecode), two MIP models (Gurobi) and an extended simulated annealing with a new neighbourhood. Instances, solutions and a solution checker are made public.
limitations: Specific real-world formulation; abstract does not state which method wins.
algorithm: Constraint programming (MiniZinc/Gecode), MIP (Gurobi), simulated annealing
benchmark: Real university instances from Italian universities (Battistutta et al. 2020)
notes: Discovered; verified via OpenAlex and Springer. Online 4 May 2023. OpenAlex author display 'Thomas Stidsen' (middle initials not confirmed). Family: CP / MIP vs metaheuristic.

title: Multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing for the ITC-2007 capacitated examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing for ITC-2007, with new neighbourhoods that exploit the disconnected structure of the conflict graph and handle exam-room assignment, tuned by a principled procedure and analysed by ablation. It competes with state-of-the-art solvers and finds several new best solutions.
limitations: Capacitated ITC-2007 only; static.
algorithm: Multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing (conflict-graph-aware neighbourhoods)
benchmark: ITC 2007
notes: Discovered; verified via OpenAlex and Springer. Online 19 Dec 2023 (OpenAlex year 2023); issue April 2025. Family: metaheuristic local search.

title: A proven optimal result for a benchmark instance of the uncapacitated examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Journal version of B20: proves optimality of the best known sta83 (Carter) solution by decomposing the problem into three parts, each closed with a different approach. It also gives optimal solutions to subproblems in public datasets and two best known solutions.
limitations: Single instance proven optimal; same work as the PATAT 2022 paper.
algorithm: Decomposition + mixed integer programming / exact methods
benchmark: Toronto/Carter (sta83); Springer page also mentions ITC-2007 and Italian instances for subproblem results
notes: Discovered while checking the B24 draft DOI. Online 11 Mar 2024 (OpenAlex year 2024); issue April 2025. Author order differs from PATAT version. Open access CC BY. Family: exact.
